questions.question: A plastic, shatter-resistant face shield protects the wearer from:

options.text: Insects.
Headlight glare.
Noise.
Sunshine.

questions.correctAnswerText: Insects.
questions.explanation: A face shield protects you from wind, dust, dirt, rain, insects, and pebbles thrown up from the road.

questions.question: Signals on a motorcycle:

options.text: Serve little purpose since motorcycles are smaller than most other vehicles.
Are very important to alert other motorists to a rider's intentions.
Should not be used if no vehicles are close to the motorcycle.
Are more complicated than those on a car.

questions.correctAnswerText: Are very important to alert other motorists to a rider's intentions.
questions.explanation: Motorcycle riders are at higher risk, so using turn signals is very important. Always use them when you plan to change lanes or turn, even if you think no one is nearby.

questions.question: Motorcycle riders should choose footwear with soles that:

options.text: Are made of hard, durable, slip-resistant material.
Allow their feet to breathe.
Have tall heels.
Are made of soft, flimsy material.

questions.correctAnswerText: Are made of hard, durable, slip-resistant material.
questions.explanation: Choose riding boots or shoes that are high and sturdy to cover and support your ankles. The soles should be made of hard, durable, slip-resistant material.

questions.question: Which of the following is not a slippery surface?

options.text: A gravel road
A patch of leaves
An ice patch
Dry concrete

questions.correctAnswerText: Dry concrete
questions.explanation: Wet pavement, gravel, sand, mud, snow, ice, painted lane markings, and metal covers in the road are all slippery. Dry pavement provides good traction.

questions.question: When checking tire pressure:

options.text: Eyeballing the tire is a good method.
Use a tire gauge.
It is best to squeeze the tire.
Compare the height of the tire to another tire.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use a tire gauge.
questions.explanation: Use a tire gauge to check pressure before every ride. A tire that is under-inflated may look fine, so looking at it is not enough.

questions.question: If your motorcycle starts to handle differently while riding, you should:

options.text: Continue riding normally.
Pull over and check the tires.
Pull over to check the chain.
Pull over to check the windshield.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull over and check the tires.
questions.explanation: A sudden change in handling may mean a tire has failed. If you feel your motorcycle handling differently, pull over safely and check your tires.

questions.question: To get the best protection, make sure your helmet:

options.text: Meets Department of Transportation guidelines.
Looks sturdy.
Is inexpensive.
Is in your favorite color.

questions.correctAnswerText: Meets Department of Transportation guidelines.
questions.explanation: Choose a helmet that meets U.S. Department of Transportation (DOT) and state standards. It should fit snugly and have no obvious defects.

questions.question: When riding a motorcycle:

options.text: It is a good idea to drag your feet.
Your toes should be pointed downward.
You should keep your feet firmly on the footrests.
You should try to keep your feet away from the controls.

questions.correctAnswerText: You should keep your feet firmly on the footrests.
questions.explanation: Keep your feet firmly on the footrests for proper balance. Do not drag your feet on the ground or point your toes down, as they may catch on the road. Keep your feet near the controls so you can reach them quickly if needed.

questions.question: When braking, you should use:

options.text: Only the front brake.
Only the rear brake.
Both brakes.
Either brake, but never both at the same time.

questions.correctAnswerText: Both brakes.
questions.explanation: Always use both brakes at the same time to stop. The brakes work best when used together.

questions.question: When passing a row of parked cars, a motorcycle operator should be prepared for:

options.text: Open parking spaces.
A motorist to unexpectedly pull out of a parking space and into traffic.
Parking meters.
Other motorists to see the motorcycle and stay out of its way.

questions.correctAnswerText: A motorist to unexpectedly pull out of a parking space and into traffic.
questions.explanation: A parked car may suddenly pull out into traffic. Ride in the left part of your lane when passing parked cars on your right. This gives you more space between your motorcycle and any hazards.

questions.question: When passing parked vehicles, motorcycle riders should watch out for:

options.text: Drivers looking for parking spots.
Cars pulling out of parking spaces.
Oncoming traffic.
Noise.

questions.correctAnswerText: Cars pulling out of parking spaces.
questions.explanation: When passing parked vehicles, be careful. A car may suddenly pull away from the curb or leave its parking space.

questions.question: When riding with a passenger, you should:

options.text: Ride faster than usual.
Ride more slowly than usual.
Start slowing down later than usual.
Try to fit into smaller gaps in traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride more slowly than usual.
questions.explanation: A passenger adds weight to your motorcycle. This means it will accelerate slower, turn slower, and need more distance to stop. Ride slower, start braking sooner, leave more space between you and other vehicles, and wait for larger gaps before crossing, entering, or merging into traffic.

questions.question: Your motorcycle's brake light is:

options.text: More noticeable than a car's brake lights.
Less noticeable than a car's brake lights.
Less important than a car's brake lights.
Easier to see than a car's brake lights.

questions.correctAnswerText: Less noticeable than a car's brake lights.
questions.explanation: A motorcycle's brake light is not as noticeable as a car's brake lights. Flash your brake light before you slow down or stop to help other drivers see that you are braking.

questions.question: The shortest and safest stops happen when you:

options.text: Use only the rear brake.
Use only the front brake.
Let the front tire lock up.
Use both the front and rear brakes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use both the front and rear brakes.
questions.explanation: The shortest and safest stops happen when you use both the front and rear brakes smoothly and gradually, without skidding either tire.

questions.question: Checking your mirrors:

options.text: Is not important.
Should only be done on long trips.
Should be part of your regular scanning habit.
Is not helpful since you cannot change what is behind you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Should be part of your regular scanning habit.
questions.explanation: Check your mirrors often as part of your normal scanning routine. Also check your mirrors before changing lanes, at intersections, and before slowing down.

questions.question: When buying a protective jacket or pants, look for:

options.text: Leather material.
Polyester material.
Light materials.
Dark colors.

questions.correctAnswerText: Leather material.
questions.explanation: Wear long pants and a jacket to cover your arms and legs while riding. Leather clothing gives the best protection.

questions.question: Crashes happen most often to:

options.text: Experienced riders.
Beginning riders.
Riders who know their motorcycle well.
Riders who have taken a safety course.

questions.correctAnswerText: Beginning riders.
questions.explanation: Crashes are most likely to happen to untrained, beginning riders who do not know their motorcycle.

questions.question: Boots or shoes should:

options.text: Be made of soft material.
Have long laces that hang loose.
Cover the ankle and provide support.
Have tall heels.

questions.correctAnswerText: Cover the ankle and provide support.
questions.explanation: Choose sturdy, tall boots or shoes that cover and support your ankles. Heels should be low so they don't catch on anything. Tuck in long laces so they don't get caught in the motorcycle's moving parts.

questions.question: For motorcycle safety, you should:

options.text: Trust that everything on your motorcycle works properly.
Check your motorcycle before every ride.
Check your motorcycle once a month.
Check your motorcycle twice a week.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check your motorcycle before every ride.
questions.explanation: A small problem with your motorcycle can cause serious issues. Check your motorcycle carefully before every ride.

questions.question: Riding with a passenger:

options.text: Usually makes no difference in how the motorcycle handles.
Is usually safe for beginning riders.
Can change how the motorcycle handles.
Is good practice to get used to different riding situations.

questions.correctAnswerText: Can change how the motorcycle handles.
questions.explanation: A passenger adds extra weight, which changes how the motorcycle handles. Only experienced riders should carry passengers.
